content:
Hello everyone,
I am considering formalizing Jean-Pierre Daboussi's elementary proof of the Prime Number Theorem, and I would like to ask for the community's advice on this project.
I am curious whether this formalization would hold meaningful value for mathlib or the broader Lean formal mathematics community. Has anyone in the community already started or completed a formalization of this proof in Lean? Compared with the existing elementary proofs of the Prime Number Theorem already formalized in mathlib, are there any unique mathematical or technical merits that make this proof worth formalizing?
Thank you very much in advance for your guidance and insights.

I don't think we have any proof of the prime number theorem formalized in Mathlib yet, elementary or otherwise; the proofs of PNT in this repository follow the classic complex analytic approach (or the Fourier-analytic Wiener-Ikehara approach), and in particular go through properties of the Riemann zeta function. There are some elementary estimates of Chebyshev type (sufficient to prove Bertrand's postulate, for instance), both here and in Mathilb, but in general elementary analytic number theory has only a minimal presence in Mathlib right now. I would imagine that going through Daboussi's proof would develop many more basic elementary estimates (with explicit constants) which would be of use.

I think this project could fit within the PNT+ project, if you are willing to open it up to the community and work with a formal blueprint, etc. But it seems also doable as a standalone project, particularly if one uses AI tools to autoformalize some of the more tedious parts of the proof.

Thank you so much for your recognition and invaluable advice! I would be delighted to bring this project into the PNT+ initiative and advance it in close collaboration with the community.
Moving forward, my first priority will be to complete the formal blueprint for this proof, and I will make the project repository publicly available in parallel. I will serve as the lead maintainer for this work, driving the full end-to-end formalization effort.
Could you please advise on what preparations I should make in advance to align with the PNT+ project's standards and collaboration workflows?

Well, if you are planning to run your own repository that you maintain yourself then not much coordination with PNT+ is necessary at this stage, but one could imagine some sort of merge later on. There may be a small amount of synergy in that some of the lemmas already proven in PNT+ (e.g., in Chebyshev.lean) could be of use to your project, but large parts of it will likely not be of much use, so importing PNT+ as a dependency doesn't make much sense (particularly since so much of it is still incomplete), but perhaps borrowing a few specific lemmas might make sense (and would perhaps make it easier to merge at some later stage, though I envisage such a merge to likely be somewhat manual (or AI-assisted) in nature as I don't think there is a technically feasible way to keep two separate projects synchronized enough (with mathlib bumps etc.) that merging is painless.

We don't have detailed style guides for PNT+ (maybe we eventually should, but this is a project that has definitely been closer to the "just get the results formalized, even if messy" philosophy rather than "the code base should be as elegant and coherent as possible", although there are some portions of it that have been polished enough to be submitted to Mathlib. Most of the stylistic concerns that have come up so far have been of a technical nature - keeping heartbeats under control, and not relying too much on dependencies that have not been heavily tested for possible security risks.

You are welcome to use this channel to post about your project, as there may be a pool of people here who would be interested in contributing, or who can advise on if there are any portions of PNT+ or Mathlib that would be useful for it.

Thank you so much for this detailed guidance! I'll share regular updates on the project's progress right here in this channel, and will reach out to the community with any questions I have as I advance the work. Thanks again for all your support!
